sources.title: NGSS 4-ESS3-2: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans
FEMA P-749, Earthquake-Resistant Design Concepts (2022): 8.1.2 Braced Frame Systems, 10.5 Seismic Isolation Systems
Physical Geology, H5P Edition (Earle and Panchuk, BCcampus), 12.5 Forecasting Earthquakes and Minimizing Impacts

note.text: In an earthquake, the ground shakes. Buildings that aren't built to handle the shaking can be badly damaged.

steps.title: Building
steps.instruction: Trace the outside of the building.

note.text: Engineers can't stop earthquakes, but they can design buildings that keep people safer when one strikes.
Each floor is held up by the frame of the building.

steps.title: Cross braces
steps.instruction: Draw an X of braces on every floor.

note.text: Diagonal steel braces make an X on each floor. They stiffen the frame so it resists being pushed sideways.

steps.title: Isolators
steps.instruction: Trace the three isolators between the building and the ground.

note.text: Isolators are thick pads of rubber and steel layers under the building. The ground can move under them, so less shaking reaches the building.

steps.title: Shaking
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows showing the ground shaking both ways.

note.text: Strong building rules, called codes, help make sure new buildings are built to be earthquake-safe.

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

targets.role: Stiffens the frame against sideways shaking.
Rubber-and-steel pad that soaks up shaking.

commonMistakes.Roof: The roof is at the very top. This part is between the building and the ground: an isolator.

steps.title: Compare solutions
steps.question: Which plan would best protect people in this building during an earthquake?

options.text: Add braces and isolators, as drawn
options.feedback: Yes. Braces make the frame stronger, and isolators reduce how much shaking reaches it. Together they help most.

options.text: Paint the building a bright color
options.feedback: Color doesn't change how the building handles shaking.
A taller building isn't safer by itself. Braces and isolators are what help.

options.text: Remove the braces to make it lighter
options.feedback: The braces stop the frame bending sideways. Taking them out makes it weaker.
